evidence.excerpt:
Large language model agents can self-improve over time by utilizing procedural
memory derived from prior task trajectories, yet the distinct utilities of memories
derived from local successes and failures remain underexplored. This work studies
this question in a realistic setting with heterogeneous streams of multi-domain
tool-use tasks and various environment constraints common in real-world scenarios.
We developDual-Polarity Memory with Periodic Maintenance(DualPM), a simple,
retrieval-free memory workflow characterized by (1) customizable reflection and
procedural memory generation from both local successes and failures within each
trajectory, and (2) periodic memory consolidation over long task streams under
a given memory capacity, preventing memory explosion. Online prequential
evaluation with fine-grained metrics reveals that failure memory more strongly
broadens coverage,

improvements are statistically significant across all three recall measures (all p≤.001 ) and final
answer accuracy (p≤.015 ) in paired comparisons across all four users. The two memory polarities
exhibit distinct utility profiles. Failure-only memory achieved significantly higher discovery and
selection recall than success-only (p=.002 and p=.018 , respectively). This pattern indicates that

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Deterministic tool-call matching metrics and the official EvoMemBench checker corroborate the reported gains independently of the LLM reflection and maintenance signals.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Deterministic environment tool execution metrics on TRAJECT-Bench, DeepSeek-V3.2 reference-based answer accuracy, and the official EvoMemBench result checker.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: LLM reflection and memory drafting/maintenance based on model-visible trajectories and tool success/failure return codes.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported experimental data support the primary claim that failure memories primarily broaden execution coverage while success memories streamline execution and precision, with combined dual-polarity memory integrating both advantages.
primary.evaluation_assessment: DualPM is rigorously evaluated via online prequential evaluation across 720 multi-domain tasks on TRAJECT-Bench using deterministic tool execution metrics (discovery, selection, usage recalls, and precision) alongside external evaluation on EvoMemBench with competitive results against established baselines.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Objective execution ground truth (tool call match recall and precision) and official external test suites on EvoMemBench corroborate headline performance gains.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Deterministic environment tool execution metrics (recall, precision, interaction turns) on TRAJECT-Bench, DeepSeek-V3.2 reference-based answer accuracy, and official benchmark checkers on EvoMemBench.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Reflection and memory maintenance performed via LLM prompts relying on visible execution trajectories and environment tool success/failure return codes.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly acknowledge limitations including reliance on single ground-truth benchmark trajectories, static domain distributions across blocks, unisolated coupling between trajectory outcomes and derived guidance, and fixed hyperparameter choices.
primary.method_assessment: The blockwise task-reflection-maintenance cycle is precisely described, detailing structured schemas for memory drafting, provenance references, and bounded capacity maintenance without providing ground truth to reflection modules.
primary.quality_rationale: The study offers a well-motivated, methodologically sound framework evaluated across diverse tasks and benchmarks with appropriate statistical testing and clear separation of deterministic environment outcomes from reflection prompts.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces DualPM, a retrieval-free procedural memory framework with periodic maintenance that separately extracts, maintains, and injects lessons from both local successes and failures across multi-domain tool-use task streams.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study offers a well-motivated, methodologically sound framework evaluated across diverse tasks and benchmarks with appropriate statistical testing and clear separation of deterministic environment outcomes from reflection prompts.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly acknowledge limitations including reliance on single ground-truth benchmark trajectories, static domain distributions across blocks, unisolated coupling between trajectory outcomes and derived guidance, and fixed hyperparameter choices.
